subject: Execution reanchor — MAP rebaseline and risk snapshot
messages:
From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@athenahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@athenahealth.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concern: acceptance window slipping — need updated MAP

Karthik,

We had a quick sync this morning with the engineering leads and procurement — we're tracking a 2–3 week drift on the acceptance window for the integration. That slippage jeopardizes our internal go/no-go by the end of July.

Can your team send an updated Mutual Action Plan with the proposed new checkpoints and any changes to the cutover acceptance criteria? Procurement also needs an updated timeline for the SOW and invoice schedule.

We need the updated MAP by EOD Wednesday so we can present to our steering committee Thursday morning.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Chen
Sr. Program Manager, Integrations
Athena Health

[Attachment: none yet]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@athenahealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: acceptance window slipping — need updated MAP

Emily —

Thanks for the heads up. We've dug into the cadence variance and assembled a short rebaseline proposal that preserves a target go-live within a 14-day window while adding a short canary step to minimize risk. High-level changes: 

- Move final acceptance from 2028-07-27 to 2028-08-10 (14-day buffer)
- Add a 48-hour canary (30% traffic) 24–25 July in your non-prod mirror, full sweep on 8 Aug
- Procurement: staggered invoice schedule (2 installments) to align with canary completion and final acceptance
- Engineering: two additional QA cycles focusing on edge-case billing flows (July 10–20)

I'm attaching a concise MAP (ATHENA_MAP_v2.1.xlsx) and a procurement timeline PDF. Laura, Ben, Camila — please review the action owners and delivery lanes; I called out three at-risk tasks in the risk sheet.

Deliverable timeline: we'll send the editable MAP and an acceptance checklist now; a one-page exec summary by EOD Wednesday for your steering committee.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0187

[Attachments: ATHENA_MAP_v2.1.xlsx (spreadsheet), procurement_timeline_v2028-06.pdf]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@athenahealth.com>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: acceptance window slipping — need updated MAP

Karthik / Emily —

Quick triage from our side after reviewing ATHENA_MAP_v2.1:

- Risk heatmap: three items rated amber->red if we do not commit to additional QA cycles (data parity, webhook order). Owners assigned in column G.
- Suggest adding a rollback criterion to the canary: automatic failover to current endpoint if error rate >1.5% for 15 minutes.
- Procurement: confirm whether Athena can accept the two-installment schedule; if not, we need to keep the July 27 milestone and build a contingency runbook.

I'll coordinate with Product and send a short mitigation note before EOD. Marking this for escalation if procurement cannot accept a shifted payment schedule.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

[Inline: flagged three risk rows; see attached MAP in Karthik's email]

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@athenahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@athenahealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: acceptance window slipping — need updated MAP

Karthik, Laura —

Thanks for the quick update and the MAP. Procurement confirmed they can accept a two-installment schedule only if the canary is successful and there is a firm rollback plan. They asked for the following to be explicit in the MAP:

1) Rollback criteria and owner (engineering lead + on-call infra)
2) Post-canary monitoring windows and SLA definitions
3) Exact billing events tied to canary completion and final acceptance

We'll take your EOD one-pager to the steering committee tomorrow. If the committee requires we hold the July 27 date, we will ask Redwood to fund a short acceptance-insurance credit to cover potential business disruption. Not an ask yet — flagging as an escalation possibility.

Emily

Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concern: acceptance window slipping — need updated MAP

Emily —

Following Laura's note and procurement's conditional acceptance, here's the operational plan I'm committing to: 

- Action owners: infra on-call (Fernando) is assigned for rollback and will be present for the canary window. Product QA (Leah) owns the post-canary verification checklist. Owners listed in the MAP.
- Monitoring: we will run 1-minute error-rate checks and 5-minute latency baselines; we will notify your team at 2x threshold immediately and auto-failover at 1.5% error rate sustained for 15 minutes.
- Billing: first invoice upon canary success (defined by checklist sign-off), final invoice on formal acceptance.

Next steps: Karthik/Laura to get the one-page exec summary to Emily by EOD Wednesday. I'll prepare the acceptance checklist and the canary runbook and share links tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
